title: Teach the reader to split two-capability requests into ordered jobs
summary: Add a rule to the reader prompt: when a request needs work of two capabilities (e.g. study the pinned source, then change code), the reading covers only the first job in dependency order and names the later job explicitly instead of silently dropping it. Audience: the user, who sees both halves accounted for, and future readers/verifiers of such jobs.

defaults_applied.how: One focused prompt rule rather than new machinery.
Add a test that the rule is in the reader prompt; cargo test and clippy clean.
Rule is prose in the prompt, marked prompt-only guidance; the budget check mechanically bounds its size.
Fixes the reader's capability-selection instruction, not the one failed job.
CHANGELOG and decision entry written for an outside reader.
Criterion checks the reader would split such a request, not just that text exists.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The fix is in the reader prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md), the only place capability choice is instructed; no new pipeline mechanism for job chaining is built.

Dependency order: a study that produces the source/claims comes before a change that consumes them; the reader picks the first needed capability and records the follow-up as a named later job in out_of_scope and assumptions.
The reader prompt has a 1,800-token budget (BudgetSet::Reader in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs), so the added text must be one or two short lines, possibly trimming existing wording.
The reading schema has no field for follow-up jobs, so the schema is not changed.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need no change.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md has a rule that a request needing work of two capabilities becomes two jobs in dependency order: the reading covers the first, and the later job is named in out_of_scope and assumptions rather than dropped.
The rule gives the concrete pattern from job 20261015-223418-qb41: a study of pinned source must precede a code change that depends on its claims, so the study is picked first.
Run `cargo test`: all pass, including the context budget check that the reader prompt stays within its token budget and a new test asserting the rule's text is in the assembled reader system prompt.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the reader rule, and docs/decisions.md records the decision with the alternative considered (a schema field for chained jobs, rejected as larger than needed).

Outcome check: for a request like 'try again on <job>' whose earlier failure needed both a source study and a code change, the assembled reader prompt instructs the reader to choose study first and list the change as a named later job, so neither half is silently lost.

out_of_scope: Building a job-chaining mechanism or a follow-up-jobs field in the reading schema
Re-running job 20261015-223418-qb41 or 20261015-214235-be8x, the firstmate re-study, or the pin-consistency check in rules.rs
Changing the capability catalog or the study/change capabilities themselves
